lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I follow George from borrowed certainty toward a city learning the news.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Saturday’s papers gave him a brief report, while their leaders comforted London.

lines.speaker: narrators_brother
lines.text: I will run down tonight.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: George sent a telegram at four, then prepared to travel south that night.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: His plan carried him from the classroom toward Waterloo and the waiting trains.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A storm brought George to Waterloo, where the Woking route had already failed.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The dark boards turned a promised journey into a fixed station view.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Windsor and Chertsey had joined Woking in the railway’s spreading interruption.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then guns and soldiers entered the station, giving the rumors military weight.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The police cleared the platform, and George was driven back into London.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: On the bridge, brown scum crossed the peaceful river beneath the sunset.

lines.speaker: unnamed_newspaper_boy
lines.text: Dreadful catastrophe!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: From Wellington Street came damp sheets, placards, and the first public cry.

lines.speaker: unnamed_newspaper_boy
lines.text: Fighting at Weybridge! Full description!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The cry carried catastrophe east.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Surrey maps spread across glass as the battlefield entered London’s streets.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Refugees carried furniture, boxes, children, and frightened fragments of news.

lines.speaker: unnamed_newspaper_boy
lines.text: Fighting at Weybridge! Full description! Repulse of the Martians! London in Danger!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: George walked north, fearing for me while ordinary promenaders continued around him.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Heavy firing crossed the city and reached George beside Regent’s Park.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He reread the paper, prowled outside, studied, and finally went to bed.

lines.speaker: police
lines.text: They are coming!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The warning changed George’s private watch into preparation for the public emergency.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Bells, feet, red light, and racing vehicles awakened the streets before dawn.

lines.speaker: unnamed_newspaper_boy
lines.text: London in danger of suffocation! Defences forced!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The morning paper carried a dispatch that turned alarm into a direction.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The dispatch made instant flight George’s only practical road.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He gathered the money that could carry him into the streets.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: George reached the doorway, while London’s panic gathered beyond the threshold.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: All six million of London were stirring, slipping, running.

lines.speaker: unnamed_newspaper_boy
lines.text: Black Smoke!
